methods.description: Answers at once: proves the node is reachable.
Returns the node's id, registry port, capacity profile, uptime, Lamport time and Java version.

parameters.name: text

methods.description: Chained SHA-256 over the node's seed, rounds times: real work done on the node.

parameters.name: rounds
parameters.description: How many SHA-256 rounds the node computes.

payloadSizeBasis: Java serialization size (java.io ObjectOutputStream, stream header included); not the RMI wire bytes; primitive parameters are sized as primitives, as RMI marshals them
lookupBasis: The time of a successful registry lookup on the calling node: one request to the target node's registry, on a new or a pooled loopback connection, plus RMI's distributed garbage collection "dirty" call to the target node, which RMI makes on the same thread before lookup() returns whenever this process holds no other live stub for that exported endpoint (always after the node exported it anew). A failed dirty call does not fail the lookup. The method call itself is not included; it is roundTripNanos.

coHosting.reason: All nodes run inside one backend process on one computer, so they are separate nodes sharing a machine, not separate machines. Every call on this page still goes through the target node's own RMI registry and a stub over a real loopback socket, so the lookup, the marshalling and the round trip are real and measured; only the network distance between the nodes is missing.

comparisonNote: Each side is a single measurement: the direct call runs first, then the same call through RMI, with no warm-up call and no averaging. The first call after the backend starts also pays for loading classes, so the direct side can be the slower one: the overhead can be negative and the ratio below 1. The figures are shown exactly as measured.

failureKinds.description: Nothing accepted the connection at the node's RMI port: the node is down or its endpoint is not exported.
The connection to the node's RMI port could not be set up: an I/O error happened while connecting.
The connection to the node broke during the call: the node closed it, for example because it crashed or restarted while RMI was reusing a pooled connection to it.
The node did not answer within the call timeout.
The stub points at a remote object that is no longer exported, for example after the node crashed and came back.
The node's registry has no entry under that name.
The call's arguments could not be written to the connection.
The reply could not be read: its data could not be deserialized.
The node could not read the call's arguments, for example because its serial filter refused them; the method never ran.
The call reached the node, and the method itself threw an exception, which RMI carried back to the caller.
Another failure; see the exception class and message.
